about: The evangelium of the formulary “Dedication of the Archbasilica of the Most Holy Savior” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus had entered Jericho and was walking through it. And behold, a man called Zacchaeus; and he was chief among the publicans, and he himself was wealthy. And he kept trying to see who Jesus was, and he could not because of the crowd, for he was of small stature. And running on ahead, he climbed into a sycamore tree so that he might see Him, since He was about to pass by that way. And when He had come to the place, Jesus, looking up, saw him, and He said to him: Zacchaeus, hurry down, for today I must remain in your house. And he hurried down and received Him, rejoicing. And when they all saw it, they were murmuring, saying that He had gone to lodge with a sinful man. But Zacchaeus, standing there, said to the Lord: Behold, half of my goods, Lord, I give to the poor; and if I have cheated anyone of anything, I give back four times as much. Jesus said to him: Salvation has been wrought for this house today, because he too is Abraham’s son. For the Son of Man came in order to seek out and to save what had been lost.
